# Kyoto 5-Day Walking Trip Plan

A relaxed, temple-forward Kyoto itinerary for 2 adults, built around walkable neighborhoods, food markets, and one true rest day. Budgeting is kept offline and conservative, with transport and admission kept light.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Route Plan

### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, then take an easy walk through Gion and Hanamikoji.
- Afternoon: Visit Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and Kiyomizu-dera area at a slow pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and Kiyomizu-dera area at a slow pace, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Casual kaiseki set or tofu dinner near Higashiyama.
- Budget note: Keep this day simple; avoid taxis unless luggage is heavy.

### Day 2: Eastern Temples and Philosopher’s Path
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Start at Ginkaku-ji, then walk the Philosopher’s Path.
- Afternoon: Continue to Nanzen-ji and nearby sub-temples or gardens.
- Dinner: Nishiki-style izakaya or seasonal noodles in central Kyoto.
- Budget note: Best full walking day; use buses only for one-way returns if needed.

### Day 3: Market Day and Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Explore Nishiki Market early for snacks, pickles, sweets, and tea.
- Afternoon: Walk to Teramachi and Shinkyogoku, then slow down at a café or department-store food floor.
- Dinner: Street-food-style grazing or a ramen counter meal.
- Budget note: This is your best day for food spending without overshooting the budget.

### Day 4: Rest Day in Arashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Late start, then a gentle visit to Tenryu-ji and the bamboo grove.
- Afternoon: Choose one low-effort stop only, such as Okochi Sanso garden or a riverside tea break.
- Dinner: Early dinner in Arashiyama or back in central Kyoto.
- Budget note: Keep activities minimal; this is the recovery day built into the trip.

### Day 5: Northern Kyoto Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit Kinkaku-ji or Ryoan-ji, depending on energy and queue tolerance.
- Afternoon: Return to the city for final shopping, matcha sweets, or one last temple stop.
- Dinner: Departure dinner or a flexible final meal near your hotel.
- Budget note: Leave room for souvenirs and one final taxi if needed.

## Map-Style Route Summary

Kyoto is easiest to plan as 4 compact walking zones plus 1 rest day:
- Zone 1: Higashiyama and Gion — temples, old streets, evening strolls
- Zone 2: Eastern Kyoto — Ginkaku-ji, Philosopher’s Path, Nanzen-ji
- Zone 3: Central Kyoto — Nishiki Market, Teramachi, dining, shopping
Media: Alt=Zone 3: Central Kyoto — Nishiki Market, Teramachi, dining, shopping, Kyoto, Japan
- Zone 4: Arashiyama — light nature walk, temple, riverside break
- Zone 5: Northern Kyoto — Kinkaku-ji and Ryoan-ji for a final temple day

Suggested flow:
- Day 1: East/southeast Kyoto
- Day 2: Northeast Kyoto
- Day 3: Central Kyoto
- Day 4: West Kyoto rest day
- Day 5: Northwest Kyoto

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

A practical offline budget split for 5 days:
- Lodging: 70,000–100,000 JPY
- Food and drinks: 45,000–60,000 JPY
- Local transit: 8,000–15,000 JPY
- Admissions and small fees: 10,000–20,000 JPY
- Buffer/souvenirs: 15,000–25,000 JPY

This keeps the total comfortably within **180,000 JPY** if you choose mid-range lodging and mostly use trains/buses plus walking.
